name: BranchSiteA_test
title: Bayesian branch-site test for positive selection

citation.title: Evaluation of an improved branch-site likelihood method for detecting positive selection at the molecular level

args.name: submodel
args.description: Codon model as a function of omega

args.name: fs
args.description: Background category proportions; one entry for each omega plus the final neutral category

args.name: omegas
args.description: Background omega values, excluding the final value fixed at 1; length(fs)-1 entries

args.name: posP
args.description: Fraction of sites switching to the foreground omega value

args.name: posW
args.description: Foreground omega for switching sites when posSelection=1; ignored when posSelection=0

args.name: posSelection
args.description: Model indicator: 0 for a switch to neutrality, 1 for a switch to omega=posW

args.name: branchCats
args.description: Branch categories: 0 for background, 1 for foreground. By default, read from tree annotations such as [&foreground=1]; unlabelled branches use 0

args.name: n
args.description: Number of background categories, including the neutral category, when omegas is not supplied; at least 1

description:
A Bayesian comparison of BranchSiteA with its null model fixing the foreground selection omega to 1, corresponding to Test 2 of Zhang, Nielsen, and Yang (2005). Background branches have, by default, a conserved category with 0 < omega < 1 and a neutral category with omega=1. A fraction posP of sites switches on foreground branches to omega=1 under the null (posSelection=0), or to omega=posW under the alternative (posSelection=1). The default prior places posW above 1 and gives each hypothesis probability 0.5.

Use n to add background categories, extending model A. Supplying omegas instead determines the category count and the default length of fs; the neutral category remains last. For random n, use --log-format=json to allow the number of logged parameters to change. The foreground and background mixtures are each normalized to mean rate 1. All component models must share equilibrium frequencies. Use a fixed topology when branch categories come from tree annotations.

The default background uses GTR, MNM, and MutSelAA. Here omega scales nonsynonymous rates after accounting for amino-acid fitnesses. Thus omega=1 retains these fitness effects; neutrality and positive selection are assessed relative to this background.

The posterior probability that posSelection=1 is the posterior probability that some sites undergo positive selection on the foreground branches.

The posterior mean of PrPosSelection can provide a more accurate estimate of this probability than the posterior mean of posSelection. The statreport tool uses LogOddsPosSelection to report the corresponding posterior log odds accurately, even when the probability is extremely close to 0 or 1. (Do not average LogOddsPosSelection directly.)
